raw: {"analysis":"HLP provides a more thorough and well-structured plan, correctly parallelizing independent workstreams (build, compliance audit, security token coordination) and clearly serializing the signing step. It also includes a smart independent technical review (diff comparison) to ensure only the data sync fix is included, and properly sequences the Director of Product's signature after signing. GRQ has a structural issue: it places manual accessibility verification in Lane B (compliance audit) which runs in parallel with the build, but accessibility checks must be performed on the built artifact—creating a dependency that GRQ doesn't acknowledge. GRQ also conflates the compliance audit and accessibility check into one lane with the Security Acting Manager, which muddies role separation. However, GRQ does a better job noting the 30-minute CI cost limit as an explicit constraint to monitor, which HLP omits entirely. Both correctly identify the Director of Product as the final approver and the acting security manager for token access.","verdict":"HLP"}
